help.text:
Run fixture-based tests defined in markdown files.

Fixtures are markdown files that define test cases using tables or command blocks.
Each file can have optional YAML front-matter for global configuration.

USAGE
  gavel fixtures [flags] <fixture-file-or-glob> [fixture-file-or-glob...]
  gavel fixtures --ui checks.fixture.md  # stream the typed execution tree in the test UI

ARGUMENTS
    fixture-files  One or more markdown fixture files or doublestar glob patterns. At least one is required.
    Quote globs when you want Gavel to expand them instead of your shell.

FILE STRUCTURE
  ---
  build: go build -o myapp           # Shell command run once before all tests
  daemon: go run ./server --port {{.port}}  # Background command run before tests; stopped after
  exec: ./myapp                      # Default executable (default: bash)
  args: [--verbose]                  # Default arguments for exec
  env:                               # Environment variables for all tests
    LOG_LEVEL: debug
  cwd: ./testdir                     # Default working directory
  terminal: pty                      # Use pseudo-terminal (merges stdout/stderr)
  setup:                             # Environment prepared once per file (see SETUP)
    dotenv: [.env.test]
    checkout: {mode: local, worktree: {mode: new}}
  record: [ansi, http]               # Capture diagnostic artifacts (see RECORDING)
  files: "**/*.go"                   # Glob pattern: replicate tests per matching file
  codeBlocks: [bash, python]         # Languages to execute (default: [bash])
  timeout: 30s                       # Total timeout for test execution
  os: linux                          # Skip on other OSes (prefix ! to negate: !darwin)
  arch: amd64                        # Skip on other architectures
  skip: "! command -v docker"        # Skip if command exits 0
  ai:                                # AI verification fixture config
    model: "provider/model"
    temperature: 0
    maxTokens: 10000
    maxConcurrent: 4
    cacheTTL: 10m
    noCache: false
  verify:                            # AI verification scoring options
    scope: diff
    threshold: 80
    disabled: [style]
  ---

FORMAT 1: MARKDOWN TABLES
  Each row defines a test. Column headers map to fixture fields:

  | Name | CLI        | Args     | Exit Code | CEL               |
  |------|------------|----------|-----------|-------------------|
  | test | ./myapp    | --help   | 0         | stdout.contains() |

  Input columns
    name, test name  Test name (required)
    cli, command, exec  Executable to run
    cli args, args, arguments  Arguments (space-separated)
    cwd, dir, working directory  Working directory
    terminal, term  Terminal mode ("pty" for pseudo-terminal)
    os  OS constraint (e.g. "linux", "!darwin")
    arch  Architecture constraint (e.g. "amd64")
    skip  Bash command; exit 0 = skip test
    record, recording  Recorders for this row: ansi, http, sql, clients, all, none
    query  Query string

  Expectation columns
    exit code, exitcode  Expected exit code (default: 0, "-" to skip)
    expected output, output, stdout  Expected stdout (literal or @file reference)
    stderr  Expected stderr (literal or @file reference)
    expected error, error  Expected stderr substring (implies non-zero exit)
    expected format, format  Output format validation (json, yaml)
    expected count, count  Expected result count for fixture types that expose counts
    expected matches, matches  Expected output/result matcher value
    expected results, results  Expected structured result value
    expected files, files  Expected file result value
    template output  Expected templated output value
    cel, validation, expr  CEL validation expression

  Unrecognized columns become Properties available in CEL.

FORMAT 2: COMMAND BLOCKS
  Use heading ### command: <test name> followed by code blocks:

  ### command: my test
  ```yaml
  cwd: ./testdir
  exitCode: 0
  terminal: pty
  os: linux
  env:
    KEY: value
  ```
  ```bash
  echo "hello world"
  ```

  YAML fields: cwd, exitCode, env, timeout, terminal, os, arch, skip, record

  Validations
    * cel: stdout.contains("hello")
    * contains: hello
    * regex: .*world.*
    * not: contains: error

FORMAT 3: AI VERIFICATION FIXTURES
  Add ai: front-matter to turn the markdown document into one AI verification step.
  The first ```prompt or ```ai block becomes reviewer instructions.
  GitHub task-list items become scored acceptance criteria.

  Example
  ---
  ai:
    model: "claude-code-sonnet"
  verify:
    threshold: 80
  ---

  # Verify feature X

  Some prose describing the expected change.

  ```prompt
  Focus on the new parser path and acceptance criteria.
  ```

  ## Acceptance Criteria
  - [ ] Parser errors are actionable
  - [ ] Existing fixture formats still pass

  - cel: json.score >= 80

  AI options
    model  Agent model name (falls back to the default model)
    temperature  Sampling temperature
    maxTokens  Maximum response tokens
    maxConcurrent  Maximum concurrent AI checks
    cacheTTL  Cache duration for AI calls
    noCache  Disable AI response cache

  Verify options
    scope  Review scope, defaulting to the working-tree diff
    threshold  Minimum passing score, defaulting to 80
    disabled  Check IDs to disable for this fixture


FORMAT 4: TEST / LINT STEPS
  A ```yaml test or ```yaml lint fence (bare ```test / ```lint also work; the
  leading yaml is optional and only there for editor highlighting) runs the test / lint
  engine. The YAML body is unmarshalled directly onto the gavel test / gavel lint options, so
  every CLI flag is available as a key (kebab-case). Each test / violation becomes a child node.

  Example
  ## Run the engine tests
  ```yaml test
  paths: [./testrunner/...]
  framework: [go]
  test-timeout: 2m
  show-passed: true
  ```

  ## Lint the changed files
  ```lint
  linters: [golangci-lint, ruff]
  changed: true
  fix: false
  ```

  Common test keys
    (full list: gavel test --help)
    paths  Package paths to test (empty = discover all)
    framework  Restrict to jest, vitest, playwright, go, ginkgo
    changed, since, failed, baseline  Narrow to changed / prior-failed / new-vs-baseline packages
    extra-args  Arguments forwarded to the underlying runner
    test-timeout, timeout  Per-package / whole-run deadline (e.g. 2m)
    lint  Also run linters in parallel with the tests

  Common lint keys
    (full list: gavel lint --help)
    linters  Only run these linters (empty = every detected linter)
    files  Target paths to lint
    ignore  Glob patterns to exclude
    fix  Apply auto-fixes
    changed, since, baseline, failed  Only report new / prior violations
    timeout  Per-linter timeout (e.g. 5m)

  Rendering
    show-passed  Add passing tests / clean linters as child nodes (default: only failures)
    show-failed  Add failing tests / violations as child nodes (default: true)

  UI / detach options (ui, addr, detach) are ignored, and a test step never
  recurses into fixture discovery.

SUPPORTED LANGUAGES
    bash, sh, shell  bash -c <content>
    python, py, python3  python -c <content>
    typescript, ts  ts-node -e <content>
    javascript, js  node -e <content>
    pwsh, powershell  pwsh -Command <content>
    go  go <content>
    test, lint (or yaml test/yaml lint)  Run the test / lint engine (see FORMAT 4)

  Non-executable labels (parsed as config): yaml, frontmatter, json

INLINE CODE FENCE ATTRIBUTES
  Attributes on the opening fence override YAML block values:

    ```bash exitCode=1 timeout=30
    exit 1
    ```

  Supported: exitCode=N (integer), timeout=N (seconds).

VALIDATION SHORTHAND
  Bullet lists after a code block define validations (joined with &&):

    cel: <expr>  Raw CEL expression
    contains: <text>  stdout.contains("<text>")
    regex: <pattern>  stdout.matches("<pattern>")
    not: contains: <text>  !stdout.contains("<text>")
    not: <expr>  !(<expr>)

TEMPLATE VARIABLES
  The exec, daemon, build, args, and cwd fields support shell-style $VAR and Go template syntax:

    exec: $executablePath
    daemon: go run ./server --port {{.port}}
    args: [--file, "$file"]
    build: go build -o $workDir/myapp
    cwd: $GIT_ROOT_DIR/testdata
    port  Free TCP port available to daemon commands and fixture templates


FILE EXPANSION
  Set files in front-matter to replicate each test per matching file:

  ---
  files: "**/*.go"
  exec: golint
  args: ["{{.file}}"]
  ---

SETUP
  setup: declares the environment a file's tests need — dotenv files, environment
  variables, cloud/Kubernetes connections, and a git checkout or worktree to run in.

  It is file-level front-matter only: prepared once, shared by every test in the file,
  and torn down after the last one finishes. A per-test setup: is an error. Because the
  file's tests still run concurrently in one group, a worktree isolates the file from the
  rest of the repository — it does not isolate the file's tests from each other.

  Example
  ---
  setup:
    dotenv: [.env.test]
    envVars:
      - name: LOG_LEVEL
        value: debug
    checkout:
      mode: local          # none | local | remote
      worktree:
        mode: new          # none | new | existing
        base: HEAD         # commit-ish to branch from
        uncommitted: clone # clone | skip — staged + unstaged + untracked
        ignored: clone     # clone | skip — gitignored content
        keep: false
    connections:
      aws: {connection: "connection://aws/sandbox", region: us-east-1}
  build: go build -o ./bin/app
  exec: ./bin/app
  ---

  Options
    cwd  Where the file's commands run (default: the markdown file's directory)
    baseDir  Where clones and worktrees land (default: a per-file dir under the user cache)
    dotenv  Dotenv files to load, resolved relative to the markdown file
    envVars  Explicit name/value (or valueFrom) environment entries
    checkout  Git checkout: mode none|local|remote, url, ref, path, connection, since
    checkout.worktree  Disposable worktree: mode none|new|existing, base, uncommitted, ignored, prefix, keep
    connections  Named cloud/Kubernetes connections; connection:// refs need a database

  Guarantees
    * The source repository is never mutated — nothing is stashed, moved, or restored.
    * Ordering is setup → build → daemon → tests → daemon stop → setup cleanup, so
      build: compiles the same tree the tests exercise.
    * worktree.uncommitted defaults to clone only when base is HEAD; branching
      elsewhere degrades it to skip with a warning, because uncommitted work is a diff
      against your HEAD. worktree.ignored defaults to clone so node_modules, .env and
      build caches come along; set ignored: skip when that tree is large.
    * $SETUP_DIR (template var and child env var) is the prepared directory, and
      GIT_ROOT_DIR/ROOT_DIR are re-rooted onto it. {{.setup}} carries commit,
      worktree, path and dirtyFiles.
    * Golden @file expectations still resolve next to the markdown, never inside the
      worktree — the commands move, their expectations do not.
    * Environment precedence, highest first: fixture env: > setup env > injected roots >
      the inherited process environment. Setup env is additive, not hermetic.

RECORDING
  record: captures the evidence a failing fixture would otherwise not have: how the
  terminal rendered, what HTTP calls the child made, what SQL it issued. Artifacts land
  in .gavel/recordings/ and their contents become CEL roots the fixture can assert on.

  Nothing starts unless a fixture asks for it — no record:, no listeners, no files.

  Surfaces
  record: http                        # one recorder
  record: [ansi, http]                # several
  record: none                        # opt out of a file-level or --record default
  record:                             # full form
    http: {mode: connect, hosts: ["*.github.com"], bodies: 64KiB, requireEntries: 1}
    ansi: {width: 120, height: 40}
    sql:  {mode: proxy, params: false}

  Also settable per test (front-matter or a Record table column) and run-wide with
  --record. A per-test value replaces the file's outright. record: none is how a single
  test escapes both.

  Recorders
    http  Proxies the child through HTTP_PROXY and writes a HAR 1.2 document
    ansi  Runs the fixture under a PTY and records an asciinema v2 cast
    sql  Proxies postgres and records every statement as JSONL
    clients  HAR of gavel's own outbound HTTP calls, which no proxy can see

  A recorder with no implementation fails the fixture rather than silently recording nothing.

  ANSI
    * Implies terminal: pty — there is no ANSI to record from a pipe. The cast plays
      with asciinema play; gavel's extras ride in the header's _gavel key.
    * Recording also tracks the settled screen, so cast.final is what a terminal would
      show at the end and cast.duplicates names the lines a redraw left behind twice.
    * maxBytes (4MiB default) caps the recorded event stream, never the fixture's
      stdout — assertions always see every byte. A cap hit sets cast.truncated.

  HTTP
    * mode: connect (default) records one entry per TLS tunnel — host, duration, bytes —
      without decrypting it. Plain HTTP is always recorded in full. mode: mitm terminates
      TLS with an ephemeral CA and is opt-in, because whether a given runtime trusts
      that CA is best-effort. The CA is never installed into a system trust store.
    * requireEntries: N turns "recorded nothing" into a red test, which is the only
      defence against a child that silently failed to trust the CA.
    * Sensitive headers (authorization, cookie, set-cookie, x-api-key, …) are blanked
      in the artifact itself. That denylist cannot be disabled; redact: extends it.
    * scope: file (default) shares one proxy across the file, so attributing an entry
      to one test is a time-slice heuristic — the file's tests overlap. scope: test
      gives each test its own proxy.

  SQL
    * mode: proxy (default) points the child at a local postgres proxy and reads a copy
      of the wire. The DSN comes from dsn:, else GAVEL_DB_DSN or DATABASE_URL;
      both are rewritten for the child, along with PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE.
    * The proxy refuses TLS, so the upstream must accept unencrypted connections —
      true of an embedded or local postgres, not of a managed cloud database.
    * mode: inprocess records gavel's own queries instead of the child's, through the
      gorm logger. It is the only way to see a fixture step that runs inside gavel,
      and it sees nothing a child process does. Bind values follow the database
      logger's own policy there, not params:.
    * params: true keeps bind values in the artifact. Off by default — bind values carry
      the row data, which is the likeliest place in a capture for a secret.

  CLIENTS
    * Records the calls gavel itself makes — GitHub, favicons, a running daemon —
      as a HAR under the clients root. A child process's traffic is never in it;
      that is what http is for. The two roots have the same shape.
    * Like sql: {mode: inprocess} it watches one process, so only one file per run
      may declare it — a second would capture the first's traffic into its artifact.
    * Bodies are off unless bodies: asks for them; the header denylist applies here too.

  Asserting
  cel: http.entries == 2 && http.errors == 0
  cel: http.requests.filter(r, r.host == "api.github.com").size() == 2
  cel: http.statuses["404"] == 1 && http.methods["GET"] == 2
  cel: cast.duplicates.size() == 0 && cast.duration_ms < 2000
  cel: sql.by_op["INSERT"] == 1 && sql.errors == 0
  cel: clients.hosts.exists(h, h == "api.github.com")

  The http root exists only when the recorder ran, so asserting on a recording that
  never happened fails on the missing variable rather than on a zero that looks like
  an answer. When it did run every key is present, so http.errors == 0 is legal for a
  fixture that made no calls. Per-request detail is capped at 200; the counts are exact.

CWD RESOLUTION
  Working directory is resolved with the following priority:

    1. Test-level CWD (per-test frontmatter or table column)
    2. File-level CWD (YAML front-matter at top of file)
    3. Prepared setup (the checkout or worktree from setup:)
    4. SourceDir (directory containing the fixture file)
    5. --cwd flag or current working directory

  Relative CWD paths are resolved from the prepared setup when the file declared one,
  otherwise from SourceDir.

EXECUTION
  Tests run in parallel with a 2-minute default timeout per test
  and 5-minute timeout for the build step. Each file's setup: is prepared
  first, so the build command — which runs once before any tests —
  compiles inside the prepared tree. A daemon command, when configured,
  starts after build, waits for its free port to accept connections, and
  is stopped after all fixtures finish; setups are torn down last.

OUTPUT OPTIONS
    -v  Show passed fixture results
    -vv  Also show executed commands
    -vvv  Also show CEL variables and stdout/stderr by default
    --show-passed  Show passed fixture results without increasing log verbosity
    --show-stdout  When to show stdout: Never, OnFailure, Always
    --show-stderr  When to show stderr: Never, OnFailure, Always
    --update-golden  Rewrite mismatched @file stdout/stderr expectations


EXAMPLES
  gavel fixtures tests.md                  # Run a single fixture file
  gavel fixtures fixtures/**/*.md          # Run with glob
  gavel fixtures -v tests.md               # Show passed fixtures
  gavel fixtures -vv tests.md              # Also show commands
  gavel fixtures -vvv tests.md             # Also show stdout/stderr
  gavel fixtures --no-progress tests.md    # Disable progress display
  gavel fixtures outline tests.md          # Parse and outline without running fixtures
  gavel fixtures --schema                  # Print the fixture/test JSON schemas and exit
FLAGS
  --addr string  Interface to bind the fixture UI HTTP server (default 0.0.0.0)
  --auto-stop duration  With --ui --detach, hard deadline for the detached UI server (default 0s)
  --detach  With --ui, keep serving the completed fixture run in a detached process
  -h, --help  help for fixtures
  --idle-timeout duration  With --ui --detach, stop serving after this long without HTTP requests (default 0s)
  --record string  Record diagnostics for fixtures that declare no `record:` of their own: ansi, http, sql, clients, all (comma-separated)
  --schema  Print fixture editor JSON schemas and exit
  --show-passed  Show passed fixture results in output
  --show-stderr string  When to show stderr: Never, OnFailure, Always (default OnFailure)
  --show-stdout string  When to show stdout: Never, OnFailure, Always (default OnFailure)
  --ui  Launch a browser with the live fixture execution tree
  --update-golden  Rewrite @file stdout/stderr expectations with actual output instead of failing on mismatch
